The iconic FINAL FANTASY XIV raid series, the Archadion, comes to musical life once again in this set of 2 vinyl records. Sit back and immerse yourself in the warm, analog versions of the songs that accompanied you on your arena trials and tribulations. For those who wish to partake in the nostalgia of battle but do not own a record player, this album also comes with a download code for MP3s of the tracks.

PSA: Final Fantasy XIV Online Free Subscription Period For Switch 2's "Full Version" Ends Next Week
items.summary: "You can continue playing the Free Trial free of charge"
items.content:
"You can continue playing the Free Trial free of charge"

Square Enix's MMORPG Final Fantasy XIV Online finally landed on the Switch 2 last month, and Square Enix has now issued a reminder that the "free subscription period" for the "full version" of the game on this platform will soon end.

This free period, which was introduced to "help ensure server stability", will end next week on 7th September 2026 .

It's further noted how the "30-day free play period granted when registering the Starter Edition or Complete Edition" will begin a day later on 8th September 2026 . When this 30-day period has elapsed, a subscription fee will then be required to continue playing.

Square Enix also mentions how users with the Free Trial download can continue to play "free of charge". Its support page expands on this: "Once your service account is upgraded to a full service account on any platform, you will no longer be able to revert back to a Free Trial account".

" The Free Trial allows you to play for free up to level 80 and experience what FINAL FANTASY XIV has to offer. ...The FINAL FANTASY XIV Online Free Trial includes four award-winning titles - FINAL FANTASY XIV: A Realm Reborn the base game, and the first, second and third expansions: FINAL FANTASY XIV: Heavensward, FINAL FANTASY XIV: Stormblood and FINAL FANTASY XIV: Shadowbringers."

You can get the full breakdown about the subscription fees for the Switch 2 version of FFXIV in Square Enix's FAQ .

items.title: ‘Dawntrail: Final Fantasy XIV Original Soundtrack’ Makes Global Streaming Debut With 66 Tracks
items.summary: Square Enix has released the complete 66-track ‘Dawntrail: Final Fantasy XIV Original Soundtrack’ on major streaming services worldwide, bringing the music from the latest ‘Final Fantasy XIV’ expansion to listeners outside the game. The collection spans the full range of ‘Dawntrail”s score, from its title theme and area music to trial encounters, battle tracks and […]
items.content:
Square Enix has released the complete 66-track ‘Dawntrail: Final Fantasy XIV Original Soundtrack’ on major streaming services worldwide, bringing the music from the latest ‘Final Fantasy XIV’ expansion to listeners outside the game. The collection spans the full range of ‘Dawntrail”s score, from its title theme and area music to trial encounters, battle tracks and music from The Arcadion: AAC Light Heavyweight raid series.

The soundtrack was created under Sound Director Masayoshi Soken and the Square Enix Sound Team, whose work on ‘Dawntrail’ moves freely between very different musical styles. Across the expansion, the score draws on tropical acoustic textures, heavy rock, brass-heavy jazz and large-scale orchestral arrangements, reflecting the shifting locations, characters and battles encountered throughout the story.

That variety is one of the defining features of the 66-track release. Rather than functioning as a single stylistic collection, the soundtrack follows the structure of the game itself, moving between expansive environmental themes and more immediate music written for combat, bosses and major story moments.

The title track “Dawntrail” provides one of the central musical identities for the expansion, while the broader soundtrack fills out the environments and encounters surrounding the new adventure. The inclusion of music from The Arcadion: AAC Light Heavyweight also brings some of the expansion’s more energetic battle material into the standalone collection.

The global streaming release gives ‘Final Fantasy XIV’ players access to the complete soundtrack through their regular music platforms, allowing the score to exist independently from the game while preserving the musical progression of the expansion.

Square Enix Music is also marking the release with the ‘Dawntrail Streaming Celebration: FFXIV OST Share Campaign’ on its official Discord server. Running through September 10, the event invites fans to share favourite tracks, discoveries and memories connected to music from across the ‘Final Fantasy XIV’ catalogue.

That fan participation fits naturally with a game whose music has become a significant part of its identity. ‘Final Fantasy XIV’ has continued expanding both its narrative and musical world through successive expansions, with Soken and the sound team using recurring themes, genre shifts and new arrangements to accompany the changing settings and emotional turns of the story.

With ‘Dawntrail’ now represented by a complete 66-track streaming release, listeners can revisit everything from its quieter location music to its most intense raid and battle themes without needing to be inside the game itself.

The ‘Dawntrail: Final Fantasy XIV Original Soundtrack’ is streaming worldwide now.

items.title: Square Enix reminds Final Fantasy XIV players that the Switch 2’s free subscription period is ending soon
items.summary: Square Enix posted an update on its official Final Fantasy XIV page today to remind players that the free one-month grace period for its long-running MMO on
items.content:
Square Enix posted an update on its official Final Fantasy XIV page today to remind players that the free one-month grace period for its long-running MMO on Switch 2 will be ending soon. Starting September 7th, 2026, players will either need to buy the “Starter” or “Complete” editions of the game, or switch over to the free-trial that limits access to certain features. If you’ve already purchased FFXIV on Switch 2, your included month of game access will take effect on September 8, 2026.

This can be a little confusing to those not familiar with MMOs, but Square Enix launched FFXIV on Switch 2 with 30 free days as a means of testing the server stability on Nintendo’s console. Technically speaking, the game doesn’t actually release until September 7th, so Square Enix wants to remind players that they’ll soon need to start paying to keep playing. MMO fees go towards server maintenance and the development of additional content, of which Final Fantasy XIV has received six major expansion packs, so this isn’t anything new. This announcement is merely a warning so that people aren’t caught off guard if they suddenly lose access.

In order to pay for access on Nintendo Switch 2, players will need to utilize FFXIV coins, as Square Enix calls them. This is a separate subscription from the PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S versions, though having dual subscriptions will net you a 50% discount for access on the Switch 2 port. Basically, you purchase coins ahead of time and use those to pay off the monthly fee. FFXIV coins can be purchased from the game’s launcher, which will redirect to the eShop for completion of the purchase. It seems a little convoluted, but I suppose Square Enix is trying to conform to standards set by Nintendo’s online ecosystem.

If you don’t want to deal with any of that, Final Fantasy XIV does have a rather generous free trial. You’re limited in certain aspects, such as losing the ability to form parties with other players, but you can otherwise experience the entirety of XIV’s story and even play through the first four expansions. It’s certainly a hell of a lot of content for the low price of $0.

Diesel has teamed up with Square Enix ‘s acclaimed MMORPG Final Fantasy XIV for a multi-faceted project anchored in the shared philosophy of “BRAVE”.

Fusing fashion, gaming culture and contemporary art, the centerpiece of the project is a 27-piece capsule collection. The lineup translates rich gaming lore into streetwear staples, spanning washed denim jackets, wide-leg denim trousers, hoodies, long-sleeve tees, graphic T-shirts and silver jewelry. Design motifs draw directly from the world of Hydaelyn, featuring imagery of Azem’s Crystal, the Mothercrystal, the Grand Companies of Eorzea and iconic Scions of the Seventh Dawn characters including Y’shtola, Thancred, Alphinaud, and Estinien.

Ranging in price from ¥11,000 to ¥207,900 JPY (approx. $69 – $1,302 USD), the collection kicks off on September 16, 2026, with an exclusive pop-up at Isetan Shinjuku in Tokyo, which will offer custom job-icon embroidery services and a 30-set limited “Scions of the Seventh Dawn Complete Box”. A wider release follows on October 2, 2026, via Diesel’s official online store and the DIESEL SHIBUYA flagship, alongside secondary pop-ups at Hankyu Umeda in Osaka and Iwataya in Fukuoka later in the month. Coinciding with the drop, DIESEL ART GALLERY in Shibuya will host a collaborative collage art exhibition by renowned artist Kosuke Kawamura from October 2 through November 8, 2026. items.title: Review: Final Fantasy XIV on Nintendo Switch 2 is the best version of the game
items.content:
I have wanted to get back into Final Fantasy XIV for quite some time. I am a massive fan of everything it offers, from the art direction to the scope of the world and adventures that are held within it. I love the way that it handles narrative within the MMO format, and the massive range of locations to visit. I really, really love the music (I went to a FFXIV symphony and everything), and just generally the very Final Fantasy design of it.

Related reading: To think that I played this for the first time way back on the PlayStation 3. My thoughts back then.

But – and it’s a big but – Final Fantasy XIV is a MMO, and MMOs do demand a time commitment, both in terms of the raw hours you plug into it, and the frequency with which you need to play. Take a big break from an MMO, and it just becomes progressively more difficult to step back into.

I tried to get back into FFXIV once when I first picked up the ROG Xbox Ally . The device handled the game just lovely, but I’m not a frequent PC player, and so at some point I put the device down, took a long break, and just… let my subscription slip again.

I am, however, a frequent Nintendo Switch 2 player. By that I mean “daily”. And so now, with the game’s little icon sitting right there on my Switch 2 home screen, I’ve been logging in for at least a little playtime every day. I’ve already made significantly more progress than I did on the ROG.

Final Fantasy XIV plays just lovely on Switch 2, to start with that important point. The console’s screen is just large enough to be able to handle the very busy interface (it’s an MMO, it’s necessary) without distracting from the core action when you want to watch the fireworks. The game’s visual engine is just now ever-so-slightly showing its age with relatively primitive character models and textures – it has been going for something like 13 years at this point – but the art direction is still as stunning as ever, and I’ve loved revisiting my favourite parts of the world from my first playthrough.

Speaking of, I have started a totally fresh character and save file (I wouldn’t even be able to track down my original avatar from a decade ago, if she still exists on servers somewhere, even if I wanted to. I can’t remember my username, password, or the email address it was attached to). I love how it’s possible to play through all the base game and early expansions with NPCs, and not rely on parties of humans for the various dungeons. If you’ve ever played a FFXIV dungeon before, you’ll know that human allies tend to… well, race through it. One of the few unpleasant memories I have from my first playthrough of Final Fantasy XIV was getting to the very final dungeon of the base game and basically missing the whole thing (and being left behind) because I was trying to follow the story. The conclusion to literally dozens of hours of play.

Now, thanks to NPCs, you can enjoy most of the many expansions and all the stories within them at your own pace. And enjoy the typically excellent music, enemy layouts and dungeon design without feeling rushed, too. I even took time to take screenshots, which is one of my favourite ways to log my adventures in this game.

There is a downside, though. Because Square Enix wants to funnel players into the later expansions where, from their perspective, all the value to the players is, they’ve taken steps to streamline the earlier parts of the game, meaning that you accumulate experience points much (much) faster, and have to do far (far) fewer quests along the way. I have been exclusively undertaking the main quest line, with no side quests, let alone grinding, and my avatar is more than twice the minimum recommended level for any given quest or boss battle.

I understand why they did this, because otherwise it would be a truly intimidating, overwhelming task for a completely new player to get up to the newer expansions, but it means that those same players don’t get to spend enough time in parts of the world to really enjoy their contribution to the whole. The major cities are fine, but you’ll fly through little town areas where previously you’d spend a gaming session or two completing all the side quests. They’re barely blips and blink-and-you’ll-miss-them moments now, which really messes with the pacing for what was previously a truly wonderfully paced game that slowly walked you from one wonder to the next.

I don’t necessarily know what the solution is there, though if it were possible, I would have appreciated the option to toggle whether I wanted the accelerating levelling on or not.

Still, that’s my only gripe. The only other minor issue is that, when it comes to the chat, the Switch’s virtual keyboard doesn’t exactly allow for the same typing speed as a proper keyboard. I don’t even know if it’s possible to connect a Bluetooth keyboard to the Switch 2, as I haven’t tried yet, but even if it were possible, that would significantly undermine the portability of the experience. Currently I haven’t been social enough in FFXIV to require the chat function much, but I can see that becoming an issue later on in the game.

Those are only minor quibbles, obviously, set against a game that is hundreds upon hundreds of hours in scope, and now in an extremely portable and accessible format. FFXIV is a hobby all by itself, and now I can embrace and indulge it in full.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Online – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition Review
items.summary: If you haven’t heard of Final Fantasy XIV by now, where have you been? This hugely popular MMO has been around for more than ten years now and is
items.content:
If you haven’t heard of Final Fantasy XIV by now, where have you been? This hugely popular MMO has been around for more than ten years now and is currently awaiting its sixth expansion, Evercold, in January 2027. Another development that you might have missed, but one that I was feverishly excited about, was the release of the fan-favourite game on the Nintendo Switch 2.

I’ve had some time with the game on Switch 2 recently; in fact, I’ve been playing Final Fantasy XIV exclusively on the platform for the last couple of weeks for my daily level grinds. I have developed thoughts about it.

Let’s get the bad things out of the way first. Yes, it does suck quite considerably that you must get a separate subscription alongside your main one (if you have one). Sure, this is at a reduced price if you have another subscription, but it does feel very cheeky. If Switch 2 is going to be your only means of playing FFXIV, however, this is an irrelevant criticism. I will pay for both, but I’m like this.

Also, this is a chunky game, as you would expect from 100s of hours of gameplay. Even if you only do the Free Trial, which runs from A Realm Reborn up to Shadowbringers, that totals around 170 hours for just the main content. As such, it totals a whopping 117GB, which is a VERY large amount of the Switch 2’s system storage. I’ve got into the habit of removing things from the console, but if you don’t, you might want to get deleting if you’re considering diving into Eorzea.

Outside of these general critiques, I did initially have problems with the keybindings when playing the game. The A button on Switch is “confirm” on Switch 2, which is conveniently in the same place as the “cancel” button on PlayStation. So, my dumb ass kept deselecting the boss and/or party members as I was trying to do the Arcadion. But a quick switch of those in the system settings has helped my muscle memory not flare up continually.

Additionally, I must admit that things can be a little small on the Switch 2’s screen in handheld mode. This is easily remedied – of course – by altering the size of the UI details in the settings. But just a heads up that, if you copy across your settings from other platforms, like I did, you will have to spend some time changing things before you can legibly see what’s on the screen.

Believe it or not, that’s it for negatives. The short story is that it runs astonishingly well on the Switch 2. Across a variety of content, except Savage Raids as I am currently in search of a new static, there was no noticeable difference for me in performance between PlayStation 5 and Switch 2. The only issue was with the load times on occasion, but the delay with loading after revival in combat has already been repaired in a hot fix.

This is the case in both handheld and docked too, with few noticeable differences in performance between the two. The only times I saw anything close to struggling was loading into busy areas such as Limsa Lominsa in handheld mode, but even then, the drops in performance were barely noticeable. This does make sense, of course, because the game originally ran on the PlayStation 3. But it’s nonetheless impressive.

Also, if different control methods are your thing (no judgement here), the Switch 2 version of the game supports the mouse mode for easy clicking around targets. This eases up one of the biggest problems with playing on a controller, which is being able to select things outside of the key cyclable options. This is not a problem in most instances. But if you’re a Healer in an Alliance Raid with some – ahem – lacklustre Healers in other parties, you will know the struggle.

As are the visuals too. These have been brought down a touch to fit onto the platform, resulting in a graphical downgrade from PlayStation 5 to Switch 2, just not one that’s as severe as I was expecting. The soft purple hues of the trees near the Crystarium, the colourful lanterns of Kugane, and the tragic beauty of Ultima Thule are all present and accounted for. The game is just as beautiful as it’s ever been, just on a smaller screen.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV is perfect for the Switch 2
items.summary: Though it has its ups and downs
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV coming to the Switch 2 is a dream come true for me; one of my favorite games now in a portable form factor. I’ve put a ton of time into the game on the system, testing just about every scenario I can think of outside of becoming a streamer and having a crowd of people follow me everywhere. Overall, I’m pretty happy with the port and can recommend it to players new and old, but I certainly wouldn’t abandon PC for this version.

The thing I and most others were curious about most was performance on Switch 2. I have bad news on that front, as you’re pretty much never going to get 60 frames per second on Switch 2 outside of certain cutscenes and exactly one area in one dungeon. It’s disappointing there’s no performance mode or anything, but you can cap your framerate to 30 in Docked Mode for more stability. Portable is also capped at 30, so you’re essentially getting parity with that aside from resolution. Your framerate can and will still dip below 30 in some situations, like running around a crowded Limsa Lominsa, but Limsa ‘tis a silly place. You can hear more about performance in this short:

As for visuals, the game looks good. Not amazing; there’s a lot of aliasing, and you can definitely tell the resolution is lower when going from 1440p or 4K on PC, but good. Resolution often screws with your custom HUD setup, which is something I was worried about here, but aside from needing to increase the chatbox font and move my job gauges a bit to the right, I was able to download my configs no problem. It moves seamlessly between portable and docked modes as well, something this version has over playing the PC version on Steam Deck.

Steam Deck might be able to hit higher framerates more consistently, but Switch 2 has it soundly beat in convenience and battery life, not to mention fan noise. I gave up playing the game on Steam Deck after Dawntrail launched, as just playing the game made my Deck scream in agony and it would go from full battery to almost dead very, very quickly. That’s at the lowest possible settings and with a lower resolution than Switch 2 offers. FFXIV will still drain the Switch 2 pretty quickly, but it’s far from the worst I’ve seen on the platform. Just make sure you don’t register for a duty at like 30% battery and you’re fine, or have your docked setup nearby.

Being able to go from portable to docked seamlessly here is fantastic, though the star of the show here really is portable mode. I love being able to do my dailies and slowly get every Job to cap while sitting on my couch, talking with my family, or just not sitting at my PC. Especially with the weather being so hot and my bedroom, where my computer lives, is basically an oven. I could even play outside on the porch if going outside wouldn’t melt me.

One of the best parts of portable mode is the touch screen. Sometimes navigating certain menus is just more convenient with a mouse-like setup, and just being able to touch the screen makes it super easy. In Docked mode, you can use either one of the Joy-Con 2 as a mouse, but I find this feature leaves a lot to be desired; both when you’re using it and even when you’re not. Playing with split Joy-Con 2, I found my fingers would often activate the mouse sensor, messing up my controls for a second or two. Playing with mouse mode… You just don’t have enough buttons to actually play the game unless you’re the kind of person who likes to click on their hotbar actions. You could plug in a Keyboard and just use one of the Joy-Con 2 as a mouse, which does allow for a left-handed mouse setup, but at that point you might as well just plug in an actual MMO mouse while you’re at it.

Another point of contention is that there’s no physical release. That’s not a big deal for Final Fantasy XIV as it hasn’t actually been on a disc in a long time, but on Switch 2 storage space is at a premium. Final Fantasy XIV will take up almost half of your console’s onboard storage at 108 GB. With Evercold on the Horizon, it’s only going to get bigger too. I actually bought a new microSD card specifically for this game, and am working on putting together a faux physical copy, complete with a game box and “cartridge” to store the SD card in. With… everything getting so expensive lately, I settled on a 256 GB card, so I’ll have to swap out the SD card to play my other Switch 2 games, which is inconvenient. You could simply keep FFXIV on your onboard storage and all other games on an SD card, which was recommended when the game launched as there were loading issues with the SD card, but I prefer to have at least some variety.

As of writing and most likely as of when you read this, Square Enix is offering all Switch 2 players a free month of the game. After that ends, you’ll need to pay an additional subscription fee to play on Switch 2 and other platforms like PC and PS5. If you just play on Switch 2, you simply pay the normal sub, but if, for example, you want to swap between PC and Switch 2 you’ll have to pay an additional half of the subscription each month. This is done through a weird currency obfuscation method Square Enix calls FFXIV Coins. You buy coins, then use them to pay for the sub.

First off, why the obfuscation? I’d really rather you just tell me up front what it costs without me having to translate and convert. There’s a reason Nintendo and Microsoft got rid of their points systems on their storefronts. Second, I know this is how Square got out of requiring players to need Nintendo Switch Online to play on Switch 2… but personally I already pay for NSO every year, and it’s overall cheaper than this weird Coin model; $50 a year for the Expansion Pak version as opposed to $70 a year by my math. That $70 doesn’t include an already existing subscription to FFXIV, by the way; that’s just on top of playing on Switch 2. I haven’t actually paid for my sub in a long time (thanks for literally paying my sub, Square!), but if I were to stop writing about FFXIV, I would be concerned about that additional cost. Being subscribed to NSO does get you an additional free teleport destination in-game… but I have teleport tickets; I don’t need that. It’s quite literally useless to me. In this situation, I’d probably just pick what I’m going to play on for that month: Switch 2 or PC.

Seeing as the Switch 2 version feels more like a nice supplement to me, I’d go with PC most of the time. In between MSQ patches, sure, I’ll take Switch 2, but if I go back to raiding or when there’s more story to play, I’d prefer the higher fidelity and framerate of my PC. I hope Square and Nintendo reconsider the choice of FFXIV Coin, because if they did, I’d shill this version as much as humanly possible. I mean, I’ll still do that for the game overall, but here I’d mostly recommend the free trial, then moving over to PC or being absolutely sure you want to play on Switch 2 forever. If FFXIV Coin wasn’t a thing, then you’d bet your sweet bippy I’d buy every expansion twice (read: once, thanks again Square!) so I could play on both platforms. For right now though, I’m pretty dang happy with this version.

items.content:
Once more, a horde of Yo-kai descends upon Eorzea! Join in the fun and get your paws on weapons, mounts, a framer's kit, and minions─including Jibanyan and Whisper! This time around, the event features three new indoor furnishings: wibbly-wobbly Jibanyan, wibbly-wobbly Komasan, and wibbly-wobbly USApyon. * This event is identical to the one previously held, with the addition of three indoor furnishing items. * If you have already completed the quest for this event, it cannot be accepted again. However, you may still earn Yo-kai Medals while equipped with a Yo-kai Watch. * During the event, Yo-kai Watches will be available for purchase from recompense officers in major cities.

Event Duration

From Tuesday, August 4, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. (PDT) / 8:00 (GMT) / 9:00 (BST) / 18:00 (AEST) to Monday, October 5, 2026 at 7:59 a.m. (PDT) / 14:59 (GMT) / 15:59 (BST) / Tuesday, 6 October at 1:59 (AEDT) * Dates and times are subject to change.

How to Participate

Speak with the poor-heeled youth on the Steps of Nald (X:9.2 Y:9.1) in Ul'dah. Upon completion of the quest, you will receive a Yo-kai Watch and Yo-kai Medallium which you can use to obtain Yo-kai Medals. * Players must be level 15 and above to start the quest. * Players must have completed one of the following main scenario quests: "The Gridanian Envoy," "The Lominsan Envoy," or "The Ul’dahn Envoy." Don't miss out on this zany collaboration event!

Rewards

Visit the special site for more details.

items.content:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3259780/ What if FINAL FANTASY had continued to push the limits of pixel art and evolved from its classic roots? The first FINAL FANTASY to join the HD‑2D lineup, FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE delivers a visually striking experience that feels both nostalgic and new, enhanced by dynamic camera angles and pixelized 3D models that make every moment more dramatic and immersive. Return to the pixel‑art world of FINAL FANTASY, evolved from its classic roots. Travel with companions bound by fate and call on Visions to aid you in battle to uncover the truth behind a force that threatens to bring everything to ruin.

Digital Deluxe Edition:

This product is a bundle that includes the FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE base game along with the Magitek & Grimoire Deluxe Pack, which contains an item that transforms your chocobo's appearance into magitek armor, an item exclusive to this pack that unlocks a certain character's Fel Meteor Limit Burst, and useful items to aid you at the start of your journey. Digital Deluxe Edition Contents: ▼ FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE Base Game ▼ Magitek & Grimoire Deluxe Pack *Images are for illustrative purposes only. Actual in‑game visuals may differ. 　 Pack Contents: 　 • Magitek Armor Key x1 　 • Archwitch’s Grimoire x1 　 • Mastery Ring x1 (Increases MRP gained in battle by a certain amount) 　 • Tent x5 　 • Mist Potion x5 　 • Mist Ether x5 　 • Phoenix Down x5 　 • Remedy x3

Pre-order Bonus: Magitek Airship & Squire Starter Pack

*Images are for illustrative purposes only. Actual in‑game visuals may differ. This set contains an item that transforms your airship’s appearance into a magitek vessel, along with useful items to aid you at the start of your journey.
